correctness.rationale: For p>1 and any real normed X, F_u(h)=||u+h||^p has one-sided derivatives and sup_{||w||≤1} D⁺F_u(0;w)=p||u||^{p−1} (radial w=u/||u|| attains upper Lipschitz bound, including zero case). If F_u−F_v is locally constant, derivatives coincide, ||u||=||v||, so norm-power difference is zero near 0; (S) on normalized distinct equal-radius vectors forces u=v. Failure of (S) on an ℓp-sum isolates one coordinate and gives local constancy of pth-power difference, so every coordinate equals; converse embeds a failed summand. The argument holds for arbitrary indices by absolute p-sum convergence. Uniform (S) of a summand passes to its ultrapowers by applying U_X(d,a)>0 to normalized representatives; if a finite sum lacked uniform (S), an ultrapower pair would violate (S), since finite ℓp-sums commute with ultrapowers. Reverse implication via 1-Lipschitz s↦(s^p+t)^(1/p) on coordinate perturbations. Two explicit ℓ1² and ℓ∞² positive-quadrant/dominant-coordinate unit pairs have equal norm germs, proving sharp universal endpoint failure. This is analytic, not based on finite experiments.
